news.title: Infantino under huge pressure after plan for World Cup sell-off sparks resignation and rebuke
news.lede: Cordeiro quits as senior adviser to Fifa president. Lamour: sell-off plan ‘defies belief and imagination’. The walls started closing in on Gianni Infantino after another dramatic day that saw one of his senior advisers resign and brought a scathing rebuke from Fifa’s own chief operating officer. Infantino is under huge pressure after his plan to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors met a tide of opposition from around the globe.

news.title: Brazil and Argentina finally reveal stance on Infantino's hated World Cup plan
news.lede: CONMEBOL announced they held talks with all South American members to decide on Fifa president Gianni Infantino’s shameless plot to flog World Cup stakes to private investors. Brazil, Argentina and the rest of the nations insisted “football always comes first” and any final decision will be based on the sport’s best interest. However – unlike Uefa, Concacaf and AFC who outright rejected Infantino‘s initiative – Conmebol asked Fifa for additional information and clarifications. The football governing body issued the following statement: “Conmebol reaffirms that its priority will always be football: its values, its people and the passion that makes it the most popular sport in the world.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.

news.title: 'Nobody is selling football!' - FIFA responds to controversy and offers explanation after Gianni Infantino's World Cup plan sparks outrage
news.lede: FIFA has issued a firm response to the mounting backlash surrounding its controversial World Cup spin-off proposal, insisting that "nobody is selling football." The governing body claims media reports mischaracterised the plans and reaffirmed its commitment to a democratic process. FIFA has officially responded to the fierce opposition surrounding its proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project. The governing body released a public statement attempting to clear up what it described as "incorrect media reports" that disrupted the planned consultation process.

news.title: 2026 World Cup: Did Football Really Win?
news.lede: Years from now, football historians will remember the 2026 FIFA World Cup not only because Spain lifted the trophy, but because it was the tournament that rewrote football’s traditional hierarchy. Brazil’s elimination by Norway, Morocco proving once again that 2022 was no coincidence, Spain’s triumph through discipline rather than star power, and the controversies surrounding the final dominated headlines around the world. A World Cup has come to an end. But this time, it was not only one team that emerged victorious.

news.title: Gianni Infantino, Fifa and the week that rocked the football world
news.lede: Plan for sale of commercial rights to World Cup causes chaos with Uefa, AFC and Concacaf leading the opposition. It has been a week that has rocked football. The news caught everyone by surprise. When reports first emerged on Tuesday afternoon that Fifa, world football’s governing body, was to launch a vehicle to control the commercial rights to the World Cup, and would sell a stake of this company to investors, even members of the central decision-making body, the Fifa Council, hadn’t known about it.

news.title: Ranking World Cup performances by Bayern Munich players
news.lede: From 1982 to 2022, every single FIFA World Cup Final featured at least one Bayern Munich player. That streak came to an end in 2026, as France lost to Spain and England lost to Argentina in the semifinals. However, that doesn’t mean that Bayern didn’t have plenty of representation in the World Cup. Today, we’re taking a look at Bayern Munich’s World Cup performances from worst to best (Nathaniel Brown and Ismael Saibari are not included as they only joined Bayern midway through the tournament).

news.title: Andy Burnham, Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, demands Gianni Infantino's immediate resignation: “He is the wrong man to lead FIFA”
news.lede: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has become the latest high-profile figure to call for Gianni Infantino to step down as FIFA president, claiming the Swiss football administrator is no longer the right person to lead world football. Burnham criticized Infantino’s controversial plans to introduce private investment into the FIFA World Cup, describing the proposal as an “outrageous suggestion”. The Prime Minister argued that football’s biggest tournament should remain centered around supporters rather than financial interests from wealthy investors. Speaking to reporters in Sheffield, Burnham said the very fact the proposal had been considered showed his concerns about FIFA’s leadership.
